average treatment effect estimation with Missing Outcome Imputation

Source: R/moi.R
moi.Rd

Estimates the average treatment effect in settings where the outcome may be missing. The treatment effect implied by a parametric imputation model is targeted directly through an efficient one-step estimator (Nordland et al., 2026).

Usage

moi(
  response.model,
  treatment.model,
  imputation.model,
  imputation.subset = NULL,
  data,
  type = c("direct", "indirect"),
  id = NULL,
  imputation.augmentation.model = NULL,
  missing.model = NULL,
  nfolds = 1,
  silent = FALSE,
  stratify = FALSE,
  mc.cores = NULL,
  second.order = TRUE,
  return.all = FALSE
)

Arguments

response.model

formula or learner object (formula => learner_glm). For the direct estimator, the outcome model for the imputed outcome \(\tilde{Y}(\theta)\)

treatment.model

formula specifying the binary treatment. Only an intercept is allowed on the right-hand side, e.g. a ~ 1

imputation.model

formula or learner_glm object (formula => learner_glm). Model \(U(X,A,Z;\theta)\) used to impute the missing outcomes

imputation.subset

character string with an R expression evaluating to a logical vector indicating the rows of data used to fit the imputation model, e.g. "!is.na(y)". The expression is evaluated in the context of data. When NULL (default), all rows are used

data

data.frame (data.table and tbl_df objects are coerced to data.frame)

type

character specifying the estimator. "direct" (default) gives the direct one-step imputation estimator, which uses no missingness model. "indirect" gives the sub-target estimator, which requires missing.model

id

(integer or character) optional subject id vector of length nrow(data).

imputation.augmentation.model

formula or learner object (formula => learner_glm); default NULL. Working model for the conditional imputation mean \(E[U(X, A, Z; \theta) \mid W, A]\). When supplied, an augmentation term is added to the imputation sub-target for improved efficiency. Only used when type = "indirect"

missing.model

formula or learner object (formula => learner_glm(family = binomial)); default NULL. Model for the probability of the outcome being missing, \(P(\Delta = 0 | A = a)\). Required when type = "indirect" and ignored when type = "direct"

nfolds

number of folds (positive integer), or a pre-specified list of fold indices where each element is an integer vector of observation indices forming a partition of 1:nrow(data).

silent

suppress all messages and progressbars

stratify

if TRUE the response.model, missing.model and auxiliary.model (if provided) will be stratified by treatment

mc.cores

(optional) number of cores. parallel::mcmapply used instead of future

second.order

add seconder order term to IF to handle misspecification of outcome models

Value

moi.targeted object

Details

The moi function implements an estimator for the average treatment effect where missing outcomes are imputed using a parametric (glm) model.

The function estimate the target parameter

$$E[\tilde{Y}| A = 1] - E[\tilde{Y}| A = 0],$$

where

$$E[\tilde{Y}| A = a] = E[\Delta Y | A=a] + P(\Delta=0 | A=a) E[U(X, A, Z; \theta) | A=a, \Delta=0],$$

and \(\Delta\) denotes the non-missing indicator, and \(U\) denotes the imputation model possibly depending on baseline covariates \(X\), the treatment \(A\), and a post randomization variable \(Z\).

Inference is based on the estimated influence function of the associated (covariate adjusted) one-step estimator.

Two estimators are available, selected by the type argument:

  • Direct one-step imputation estimator (type = "direct", the default): targets \(E[\tilde{Y}(\theta) | A = a]\) directly via a (covariate augmented) one-step estimator applied to the imputed outcome \(\tilde{Y} = \Delta Y + (1-\Delta) U(X,A,Z;\theta)\), see supplementary material C of Nordland et al. (2026).

  • Sub-target (indirect) estimator (type = "indirect"): estimates the three sub-target parameters \(E[\Delta Y | A=a]\), \(P(\Delta=0 | A=a)\) and \(E[U(X,A,Z;\theta) | A=a, \Delta=0]\) separately and combines them. A missingness model is required for (augmented) estimation of \(P(\Delta=0 | A=a)\) and for the optional imputation model augmentation, see supplementary material B of Nordland et al. (2026).

References

Nordland, A., Holst, K. K., Redek, D., Pipper, C. B. & Iversen, A. T. (2026) One-step Outcome Imputation: An Alternative to Multiple Imputation. arXiv: https://arxiv.org/abs/2606.07174.

Author

Andreas Nordland

Examples

sim_moi <- function(n = 1000, ...) {
  w <- rnorm(n)
  a <- rbinom(n, 1, 0.5)
  y <- 1 + a + w + rnorm(n)
  ## outcome observed (delta = 1) with probability depending on w
  delta <- rbinom(n, 1, lava::expit(1 + w))
  y[delta == 0] <- NA
  data.frame(y, a, w)
}

d <- sim_moi(1000)
## direct one-step imputation estimator
moi(response.model = y ~ a + w,
    treatment.model = a ~ 1,
    imputation.model = y ~ a + w,
    imputation.subset = "!is.na(y)",
    data = d)
#> Error in ic_theta[, 1]: incorrect number of dimensions

## sub-target estimator
moi(response.model = y ~ a + w,
    treatment.model = a ~ 1,
    imputation.model = y ~ a + w,
    imputation.subset = "!is.na(y)",
    missing.model = ~ a + w,
    data = d,
    type = "indirect")
#>                       Estimate Std.Err   2.5% 97.5%    P-value
#> E[ỹ(1)]                 1.9258 0.06130 1.8056 2.046 1.355e-216
#> E[ỹ(0)]                 1.0066 0.06168 0.8857 1.127  7.021e-60
#> [E[ỹ(1)]] - [E[ỹ(0)]]   0.9191 0.07466 0.7728 1.065  7.950e-35
